title: Econ Sparker: dynamic prefill heuristics and lightweight quant profiles
author: Aisha Munroe
ci_checks: perf-benchmark: warn (1.2% regression in p99 on small-RoBERTa)
description: Motivation: large fleets pay a measurable tax for conservative cold-prefill and conservative quant choices. This change introduces the 'Econ Sparker' — a lightweight dynamic prefill controller plus a companion set of lightweight quantization profiles and telemetry hooks to reduce per-token cost while keeping latency SLOs intact. Design summary: a probe-driven, budget-aware prefill loop that samples a small number of requests (probe samples) to estimate effective warmup benefit, applies a compact micro-prefill when beneficial, and chooses a lightweight quant profile (int4-lite / 4-bit-perf) only for the prefilling execution path. The controller is latency-SLO-aware and will back off to full-safe prefill when p99 or cpu/gpu utilization signals are near configured thresholds. Implementation details: added serve/prefill/sparker.py which contains the probe scheduler, budget estimator, and a simple state machine; a new policy schema serve/prefill/policy_config.yaml to express microbudgets and SLO knobs; lightweight quant presets in serve/quant/light_profiles.json that are intentionally conservative and intended only for prefill passes; metrics in telemetry/prefill_metrics.md and instrumentation in runtime/telemetry/prefill_emitter.go. Safety and rollout: default state is opt-in; the console exposes a canary toggle and budget sliders; canary policy deployed to a small dedicated pool (canary:d-prefill-1). We included unit/integration tests and a perf smoke that gates obvious regressions. Expected impact: for chat-like workloads with prefix reuse we expect 6–18% reduction in token-unit cost on average for cold-cold flows and a negligible change in p95 latency when canaried correctly. Follow-ups: auto-tuning heuristics, richer confidence intervals for the probe estimator (ENG-1293), and a dashboard query bundle for the Console. Links: Linear ENG-1293, internal RFC: /docs/rfcs/econ-sparker.md. How to test locally: run tools/bench/prefill_smoke.py against local minimal runtime; toggle feature via console and observe telemetry.prefill.prefill_success_rate and telemetry.prefill.sampler_cost_estimate. Rollout notes: squash-merge, canary for two weeks, then evaluate cost-savings telemetry and expand.

review_comments: Diego Ramos (reviewer): The probe sampling rate looks reasonable but can we expose a conservative lower bound so very spiky workloads never under-prefill? Requested: add max_probe_delay and a unit test that simulates bursty arrivals.
Author (Aisha): Added max_probe_delay with default 1200ms and unit test bursty_probe in tests/prefill/test_sparker.py — see commit 'probe: add max_probe_delay'.

Lina Patel (reviewer): Need clearer telemetry around fallback events (when we decide to bail to safe prefill). Please add an enumerated metric for fallback_reason and a label for current_quant_profile.
Author (Aisha): Added telemetry.prefill.fallback_reason and telemetry.prefill.quant_profile label; updated telemetry doc with sample queries.
Samir Chen (approver): Verified canary run for 72h on d-prefill-1, cost delta looks promising and p95 remained within 0.6% of baseline. Approving for merge after small lint fix (done).
CI Bot: perf-benchmark reported a minor p99 regression on small-roberta. We gated with a perf threshold and author added a config to run full prefill for that model as exception.
Release Manager: Please include release notes about opt-in nature and the canary toggle.

release_notes:
- Added Econ Sparker: opt-in dynamic prefill controller that reduces cold-prefill cost using probe-driven micro-prefills.
- Introduced conservative lightweight quant profiles used only during prefill paths.
- New telemetry: telemetry.prefill.* and dashboard bundle.
- Opt-in canary (deploy/canaries/prefill-canary.yaml); default off for all tenants.
